'''Danilo Gallinari''' ({{IPA|it|daˈniːlo ɡalliˈnaːri}}; born 8 August 1988) is an Italian former professional [[basketball]] player who played 14 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). After spending his first four years as a professional in his native Italy, Gallinari was drafted sixth overall in the [[2008 NBA draft]] by the [[New York Knicks]]. He played with the Knicks for two and a half seasons before being traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in 2011.

Over the course of 16 seasons in the NBA, Gallinari also played for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], the [[Atlanta Hawks]], the [[Washington Wizards]], and the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Know The Prospect: Danilo Gallinari|url=http://www.stopmikelupica.com/2008/05/know_the_prospect_danilo_galli.php|publisher=Stop Mike Lupica|access-date=18 December 2010|archive-date=5 September 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100905222346/http://www.stopmikelupica.com/2008/05/know_the_prospect_danilo_galli.php|url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Casalpusterlengo (2004–2005)===
Gallinari started playing professionally in 2004<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=KRD |title=Danilo Gallinari |publisher=Euroleague.net |date=1988-08-08 |access-date=2012-01-23}}</ref> for Casalpusterlengo, a team in [[Serie B Basket|Serie B1]] ([[Italian basketball league system|third level in Italy]]).

===Edimes Pavia (2005–2006)===
In 2005, Gallinari was acquired by [[Olimpia Milano|Armani Jeans Milano]], which then sent him to [[Nuova Pallacanestro Pavia|Edimes Pavia]], a team competing in the [[LegADue|Italian league second division]] championship during the 2005–2006 season, so that he could earn more experience with extended playing minutes. Even though he played only half of the season due to an injury, in 2006, he was nominated as the best Italian player of the Italian league second division championship, averaging 14.3 points, 3.4 rebounds, 2.0 steals, and 0.8 assists in 17 games.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.legaduebasket.it/player/?id=GAL-DAN-88 |title=LegaDue page on Gallinari |publisher=Legaduebasket.it |date=2006-06-30 |access-date=2012-01-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120212205457/http://www.legaduebasket.it/player/?id=GAL-DAN-88 |archive-date=2012-02-12 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Olimpia Milano (2006–2008)===
In 2006, Gallinari was recalled by [[Olimpia Milano]] to play in the 2006–07 [[Lega Basket Serie A|Serie A]] season and also in the [[ULEB Cup]]. In his first season in Serie A, Gallinari was named as the league's best player under the age of 22, averaging 10.9 points, 4.0 rebounds, 1.7 steals, and 1.0 assists per game in 34 regular season games and 11.5 points, 3.7 rebounds, 2.1 steals, and 0.9 assists per game in 8 playoff games.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://195.56.77.208/player/?id=GAL-DAN-88&team=1120 |title=LegaA page on Gallinari |publisher=195.56.77.208 |access-date=2012-01-23 |archive-date=4 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120204082557/http://195.56.77.208/player/?id=GAL-DAN-88&team=1120 |url-status=dead }}</ref> During the season, he also won the 2007 Italian All-Star Game 3-point shootout contest.

He spent his last season with Milano in the top Italian league,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://195.56.77.208/player/?id=GAL-DAN-88 |title=Lega A page on Gallinari |publisher=195.56.77.208 |access-date=2012-01-23 |archive-date=22 January 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120122014446/http://195.56.77.208/player/?id=GAL-DAN-88 |url-status=dead }}</ref> finishing first in the league's overall efficiency ratings.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://195.56.77.208/rank/index.phtml?serie=1&from=2007&to=2007&sea=regular&q1=2&l=20 |title=Top 20 position |publisher=195.56.77.208 |access-date=2012-01-23 |archive-date=14 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120214174254/http://195.56.77.208/rank/index.phtml?serie=1&from=2007&to=2007&sea=regular&q1=2&l=20 |url-status=dead }}</ref> During the 2007–2008 season, he averaged 17.5 points, 5.6 rebounds, 2.0 steals, and 1.3 assists per game in 33 regular season games and 18.1 points, 6.5 rebounds, 1.8 steals and 1.5 assists per game in 8 playoff games.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://195.56.77.208/player/?id=GAL-DAN-88&team=1139 |title=LegaA page on Gallinari |publisher=195.56.77.208 |access-date=2012-01-23 |archive-date=4 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120204083243/http://195.56.77.208/player/?id=GAL-DAN-88&team=1139 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In the 2007–08 season, he played for the first time in the [[EuroLeague]], where he averaged 14.9 points, 4.2 rebounds, 1.7 assists, and 1.5 steals per game in 11 games. He posted a season-high 27 points against [[Maccabi Tel Aviv (basketball)|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] in his final game,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=KRD |title=Euroleague page on Gallinari |publisher=Euroleague.net |date=1988-08-08 |access-date=2012-01-23}}</ref> and at the end of the season was named the EuroLeague's [[EuroLeague Rising Star|Rising Star]].

===New York Knicks (2008–2011)===
Gallinari's contract with [[Olimpia Milano]] had an [[escape clause]] for playing professionally in the United States, effectively eliminating major encumbrances that would have prevented him from joining the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). On 23 April 2008, he decided to declare himself eligible for the [[2008 NBA draft]]. Gallinari signed an endorsement deal with [[Reebok]] before being drafted into the NBA. He has his own sneaker, made by Reebok, called "The Rooster."<ref>{{cite news |last=Littmann |first=Chris |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/blog/the_sporting_blog/entry/view/8677/firstcuts_reebok_inks_gallinari,_debuts_shoe |title=FirstCuts: Reebok Inks Gallinari, Debuts Shoe |work=Sporting News |date=2008-06-27 |access-date=2010-12-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100213022755/http://www.sportingnews.com/blog/the_sporting_blog/entry/view/8677/firstcuts_reebok_inks_gallinari,_debuts_shoe |archive-date=2010-02-13 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

[[File:Danilo Gallinari Knicks 2010.jpg|thumb|left|Gallinari training with the Knicks]]
Gallinari was drafted sixth overall in the 2008 draft by the [[New York Knicks]]. He then signed a two-year contract with the team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3479069 |title=Knicks sign Gallinari |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=2008-07-08 |access-date=2012-01-23}}</ref>

Just one game into the 2008–09 season, it was announced that Gallinari would most likely miss most of the remainder of the season due to back problems.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/basketball/knicks/2008/11/12/2008-11-12_danilo_gallinaris_back_future_up_in_air.html |title=Danilo Gallinari's back, future up in air |publisher=Nydailynews.com |date=2008-11-12 |access-date=2012-01-23 |archive-date=2 January 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110102082307/http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/basketball/knicks/2008/11/12/2008-11-12_danilo_gallinaris_back_future_up_in_air.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Despite his back problems, he came back into play on 17 January, during a game the Knicks lost to [[Philadelphia Sixers|Philadelphia]]. On 4 March, Gallinari scored a season-high 17 points against the [[Atlanta Hawks]], shooting 4–5 on three-point field goal attempts.

On 23 October 2009, the Knicks picked up Gallinari's contract option.<ref name="gallinaricontractoption">{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2009/news/10/23/knicks.moves.ap/index.html |title=Knicks pick up options on Chandler, Gallinari|work=NBA.com|date=2009-10-23}}</ref>

With the Knicks freeing up roster space for Gallinari with the trade of [[Quentin Richardson]], and with [[Al Harrington]] being relegated to the bench, head coach [[Mike D'Antoni]] named Gallinari a starter two games into the 2009 NBA season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/truehoop/post/_/id/10220/lineup-change-for-knicks-gallinari-in-harrington-out |title=Lineup change for Knicks: Gallinari in; Harrington out |work=ESPN |access-date=2010-12-18}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Alan|last=Hahn|url=http://www.newsday.com/blogs/sports/the-knicks-fix-1.812055/gallinari-will-start-harrington-to-the-bench-1.1558524 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091107183726/http://www.newsday.com/blogs/sports/the-knicks-fix-1.812055/gallinari-will-start-harrington-to-the-bench-1.1558524 |url-status=dead |archive-date=7 November 2009 |title=Gallinari will start; Harrington to the bench |publisher=Newsday.com |date=2009-10-31 |access-date=2010-12-18}}</ref> On 31 October 2009, the third game of the 2009 season, Gallinari scored a career-high 30 points and made eight three-pointers in an [[Overtime (sports)#Basketball|overtime]] loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], one short of tying a Knicks franchise record held by [[Latrell Sprewell]] and [[John Starks (basketball)|John Starks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20091031/PHINYK/boxscore.html |title=Sixers Knicks Boxscore |work=NBA.com |access-date=2010-12-18}}</ref> Gallinari set a new career high on 6 April 2010, with 31 points in a 104–101 win over the Boston Celtics.<ref>{{cite news|last=Hahn|first=Alan|title=Gallinari's 31 points lead Knicks over Celtics|work=Newsday|date=2010-04-06|url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/basketball/knicks/gallinari-s-31-points-lead-knicks-over-celtics-1.1850021|access-date=2020-09-14}}{{dead link|date=May 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

===Denver Nuggets (2011–2017)===
[[File:Lakers vs Nuggets 2013-01-06 (28).JPG|thumb|right|upright|Gallinari shooting a free throw for the Denver Nuggets in 2013]]
On 22 February 2011, Gallinari was traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in a three-team trade, which also involved the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], that brought [[Carmelo Anthony]] and [[Chauncey Billups]] to New York.<ref>{{cite web | title = Nuggets acquire five players, three picks in three-team trade | url = http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets_trade_02_22_2011.html | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = 2011-02-22 | access-date = 2011-02-23}}</ref> In just his second game with the Nuggets, he almost matched his career high with a 30-point effort in an overtime loss against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].

During the [[2011 NBA lockout]] he returned to [[Italy]] to play for [[Olimpia Milano|Emporio Armani Milan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2011-12-signings/i/87471/5611/armani-milan-brings-gallinari-home |title=ARMANI MILAN brings Gallinari home |publisher=Euroleague.net |date=2011-09-20 |access-date=2012-01-23}}</ref> On 25 January 2012, Gallinari signed a four-year, $42 million contract extension with the Nuggets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/gallinari_contract_01_25_2012.html |title=Nuggets sign Danilo Gallinari to contract extension |work=NBA.com |date=25 January 2012 |access-date=22 January 2014}}</ref> On 5 April 2013, it was announced that Gallinari would miss the remainder of the 2012–13 season because of an ACL injury.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/9138831/danilo-gallinari-denver-nuggets-season-torn-acl Danilo Gallinari out for season]</ref> The same injury forced him out of the entire 2013–14 season as well.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-f-danilo-gallinari-undergoes-knee-surgery Denver Nuggets F Danilo Gallinari Undergoes Knee Surgery]</ref>

On 29 October 2014, Gallinari made his return for the Nuggets, scoring seven points on 1-of-8 shooting in a season opening win over the Detroit Pistons.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141029/DETDEN/gameinfo.html |title=Nuggets open with 89-79 win over Pistons |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2014-10-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150125170633/http://www.nba.com/games/20141029/DETDEN/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2015-01-25 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On 22 March 2015, Gallinari scored a career-high 40 points on 12-of-21 shooting in a 119–100 win over the Orlando Magic.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150322/DENORL/gameinfo.html |title=Gallinari scores 40, Nuggets beat Magic 119-100 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2015-03-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150323100309/http://www.nba.com/games/20150322/DENORL/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2015-03-23 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Gallinari later eclipsed his career high with 47 points in a double overtime loss to the Dallas Mavericks on 10 April.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150410/DALDEN/gameinfo.html |title=Felton lifts Mavs to 144-143 win over Nuggets in 2 OTs |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2015-04-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150413093605/http://www.nba.com/games/20150410/DALDEN/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2015-04-13 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 3 August 2015, Gallinari signed a two-year, $34 million contract extension with the Nuggets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-extend-danilo-gallinari|title=Nuggets Extend Danilo Gallinari|work=NBA.com|date=3 August 2015|access-date=3 August 2015}}</ref> On 17 November 2015, he scored a season-high 32 points in a 115–98 win over the New Orleans Pelicans.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20151117/DENNOP/gameinfo.html Gallinari scores 32 to lead Nuggets past Pelicans, 115-98]</ref> On 5 February 2016, he set a new season high with 33 points in a 115–110 win over the Chicago Bulls.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160205/CHIDEN/gameinfo.html |title=Nuggets rally for win after Bulls lose Butler to injury |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2016-04-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160401182618/http://www.nba.com/games/20160205/CHIDEN/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2016-04-01 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Gallinari missed the final 22 games of the season due to an ankle injury.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/gallida01/gamelog/2016/ Danilo Gallinari 2015-16 Game Log]</ref> On 9 April 2017, Gallinari scored 22 of his season-high 34 points in the third quarter of the Nuggets' 106–105 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900576|title=Westbrook sets triple-double record, Thunder beat Nuggets|work=ESPN.com|date=9 April 2017|access-date=9 April 2017}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Clippers (2017–2019)===
On 6 July 2017, the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] signed Gallinari to a three-year, $64.8 million contract via sign-and-trade with the Denver Nuggets as part of a three-team trade that sent [[Jamal Crawford]], [[Diamond Stone]] and the Clippers' 2018 protected first round draft pick (via Houston) to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] and a 2019 second round draft pick from Atlanta (via Washington) to Denver.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/clippers-acquire-danilo-gallinari|title=Press Release: L.A. Clippers Acquire Danilo Gallinari|work=NBA.com|date=6 July 2017|access-date=6 July 2017}}</ref> In his debut for the Clippers in their season opener on October 19, Gallinari scored 11 points in a 108–92 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974442|title=Deflated Ball: Blake gets 29 in Clips' 108-92 rout of Lakers|work=ESPN.com|date=19 October 2017|access-date=20 October 2017}}</ref> On 6 December, Gallinari returned to action against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] after missing a month due to a glute injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975113|title=Towns lead Timberwolves past sinking Clippers 113-107|work=ESPN.com|date=6 December 2017|access-date=7 December 2017}}</ref> On 20 December, he was ruled out until at least January with a partial tear of his left glute muscle.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975216|title=Clippers lead all the way in beating Suns 108-94 to end skid|work=ESPN.com|date=20 December 2017|access-date=20 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2017/12/20/la-clippers-danilo-gallinari-diagnosed-partial-tear-glute-muscle/#/|title=L.A. Clippers forward Danilo Gallinari diagnosed with partial tear in glute muscle|work=NBA.com|date=20 December 2017|access-date=20 December 2017}}</ref> On 5 February 2018, he scored 28 points in a 104–101 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975541|title=Kings score 9 in 1st, rally to beat Bulls 104-98|work=ESPN.com|date=5 February 2018|access-date=6 February 2018}}</ref> On 27 February, he was once again ruled out due to a non-displaced fracture to his right hand.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/clippers/la-sp-clippers-gallinari-20180227-story.html|title=Clippers' Danilo Gallinari out with injured right hand|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=27 February 2018}}</ref>

In March 2019, Gallinari scored 20 or more points in nine straight games, marking the best scoring streak of his career.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071768|title=Clippers win fifth straight, beat Knicks 124-113|work=ESPN.com|date=24 March 2019|access-date=24 March 2019}}</ref>

===Oklahoma City Thunder (2019–2020)===
On 10 July 2019, the Clippers traded Gallinari, [[Shai Gilgeous-Alexander]], five first-round draft picks, and the rights to swap two other first-round picks to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] for [[NBA All-Star]] player [[Paul George]].<ref>{{cite press release|title=L.A. Clippers Acquire Six-Time NBA All-Star Paul George|date=10 July 2019|publisher=Los Angeles Clippers|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/clippers-acquire-six-time-nba-all-star-paul-george|access-date=10 July 2019}}</ref> On 4 August 2019, it was reported that Gallinari underwent an appendectomy.<ref>{{cite web|title=Italy's Danilo Gallinari undergoes appendectomy while preparing for FIBA World Cup
|date=4 August 2019|publisher=Los Angeles Clippers|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2019/08/04/danilo-gallinari-appendectomy-fiba-world-cup|access-date=4 August 2019}}</ref>

===Atlanta Hawks (2020–2022)===
[[File:Danilo Gallinari (51637105268).jpg|thumb|230px|Gallinari with the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in 2021]]
On 24 November 2020, Gallinari signed a three-year, $61.4 million contract with the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for a conditional 2025 second-round pick in a sign-and-trade deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-acquire-forward-danilo-gallinari|title=Atlanta Hawks Acquire Forward Danilo Gallinari|work=NBA.com|date=24 November 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Daniels|first=Tim|title=Danilo Gallinari, Hawks Agree to 3-Year, $61.5M Contract|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2866687-danilo-gallinari-hawks-agree-to-3-year-615m-contract|access-date=2020-11-23|website=Bleacher Report|language=en}}</ref> On February 24, 2021, Gallinari scored 38 points and hit a career-high and Hawks record 10 threes against the Celtics. During Game 7 of the [[2021 NBA playoffs|2021 Eastern Conference Semifinals]] against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], Gallinari came up in the final minute with a key steal from [[Joel Embiid]] and a dunk, extending Atlanta's lead to six, as the Hawks reached their first Eastern Conference Final since 2015 and only their second since moving to Atlanta in 1968.<ref>{{Cite web|author=The Athletic Staff|title=Hawks hold off 76ers to advance to conference finals behind Kevin Huerter's 27|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4208960/2021/06/21/hawks-hold-off-76ers-to-advance-to-conference-finals-behind-kevin-huerters-27/|access-date=2021-06-21|website=The Athletic|language=en}}</ref>

=== Boston Celtics (2022–2023) ===
On 30 June 2022, Gallinari was traded, alongside multiple future first-round picks, to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in exchange for [[Dejounte Murray]] and [[Jock Landale]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Completes Trade with San Antonio Spurs; Acquires Dejounte Murray and Jock Landale in Exchange for Danilo Gallinari and Future First Round Draft Picks |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-acquire-all-star-guard-dejounte-murray |access-date=June 30, 2022 |website=NBA}}</ref> On 8 July, Gallinari was waived by the Spurs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Antonio Spurs Waive Veteran Forward |url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/news/san-antonio-spurs-officially-waive-danilo-gallinari-who-was-traded-for-dejounte-murray-this-offseason-gallinari-played-for-denver-nuggets-new-york-knicks-los-angeles-clippers-oklahoma-city-thunder-atlanta-hawks |access-date=July 9, 2022 |website=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> On 12 July 2022, Gallinari signed a two-year, $13.3M deal with the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title= Danilo Gallinari agrees to 2-year deal with Boston Celtics |url=https://www.nba.com/news/danilo-gallinari-agrees-to-2-year-deal-with-boston-celtics |access-date=2022-07-11 |website=nba.com |date=July 12, 2022 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Celtics Sign Gallinari |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-gallinari |date=July 12, 2022 |access-date=July 16, 2022 |website=NBA}}</ref> On September 2, Gallinari suffered a torn [[anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] in his left knee, and missed the entire season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Celtics' Danilo Gallinari diagnosed with torn ACL in left knee|url=https://www.nba.com/news/danilo-gallinari-suffers-torn-acl |first1=Kyle |last1=Hightower |date=September 2, 2022 |access-date=June 16, 2023|website=nba.com|language=en}}</ref> As a result of his injury, and a trade preceding the 2023–24 season, Gallinari was not able to see the court during his time with the [[Boston Celtics]].

===Washington Wizards (2023–2024)===
On 23 June 2023, the Celtics traded Gallinari to the [[Washington Wizards]] as part of a three–team deal involving the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. The Wizards received Gallinari, [[Mike Muscala]], and the No.35 overall pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]] from Boston as well as [[Tyus Jones]] from Memphis in exchange for [[Kristaps Porziņģis]] who landed in Boston. Additionally, Boston received the No. 25 overall pick in the 2023 NBA draft and a 2024 first round pick (via [[Golden State Warriors|GSW]]) from Memphis, while the Grizzlies acquired [[Marcus Smart]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Wizards Acquire Three Veteran Players in Three-Team Deal|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-aquire-three-veteran-players-in-three-team-deal|website=NBA.com|date=23 June 2023|access-date=23 June 2023}}</ref>

===Detroit Pistons (2024)===
On 14 January 2024, Gallinari was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]], along with [[Mike Muscala]], in exchange for [[Marvin Bagley III]], [[Isaiah Livers]] and future draft considerations.<ref>{{cite web|title=DETROIT PISTONS ACQUIRE DANILO GALLINARI AND MIKE MUSCALA|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-acquire-danilo-gallinari-and-mike-muscala|website=NBA.com|date=14 January 2024|access-date=14 January 2024}}</ref> On 9 February, he was waived by the Pistons.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Pistons PR|title=The Detroit Pistons announced today that the team has requested waivers on forward Danilo Gallinari.|number=1756134846597116183|user=Pistons_PR|date=February 9, 2024|access-date=February 9, 2024}}</ref>

===Milwaukee Bucks (2024)===
On February 21, 2024, Gallinari signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Danilo Gallinari|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-danilo-gallinari|website=NBA.com|date=21 February 2024|access-date=22 February 2024}}</ref>

===Vaqueros de Bayamón (2025)===
On 22 January 2025, Gallinari signed with the [[Vaqueros de Bayamón]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Alessandro|last=Maggi|title=Shocking Move: Danilo Gallinari Signs with Vaqueros de Bayamón in Puerto Rico|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/shocking-move-danilo-gallinari-signs-with-vaqueros-de-bayamon-in-puerto-rico/|website=Sportando.basketball|date=22 January 2025|access-date=22 January 2025}}</ref> On 12 August, Gallinari led the Vaqueros to their 17th title, granting him the honors of Finals MVP.

On 2 December 2025, Gallinari announced his retirement from professional basketball.

==National team career==
[[File:Danilo Gallinari.jpg|thumb|Gallinari with Italy in 2012]]
Gallinari was a member of the Under-16 and Under-18 Italian national teams. He played at the [[2004 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]] and won the bronze medal at the [[2005 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]]. He was later selected for the [[Italy national basketball team|senior national team]] to play in [[EuroBasket 2007]], but was forced to withdraw due to an injury that he suffered in preparation before the tournament. He was called up to the squad that would take part in [[EuroBasket 2015]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/season_2015.coid_s,Z8kZaZIlsLwQFktgGes0.articleMode_on.html |title=Italy take their dream roster to Berlin |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=2 September 2015 |website=[[FIBA Europe|FIBAEurope]].com |access-date=2 September 2015}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Gallinari's father, [[Vittorio Gallinari]], played professional basketball with [[Olimpia Milano]] (along with future head coach [[Mike D'Antoni]]),<ref>{{cite web|last=Thomas|first=Ian|title=World of Ability|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/writers/ian_thomsen/01/31/gallinari/|work=Sports Illustrated|access-date=2011-10-20|archive-date=22 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121022234009/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/writers/ian_thomsen/01/31/gallinari/|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Pallacanestro Pavia]], [[Virtus Bologna]], and [[Scaligera Basket Verona]] in the [[Serie A (basketball)|Italian league]].

According to multiple sources, before [[Kim Kardashian]] began dating [[Kris Humphries]], she was extremely interested in dating Gallinari, who was told that such a move would be good for his career and that he would garner lots of media exposure. Gallinari declined, saying he would be happy to meet Kardashian but wasn't interested in dating her.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cbsnews.com/losangeles/news/kim-kardashian-wanted-italian-gallinari-first-not-husband-kris-humphries/ | title=Kim Kardashian Wanted Italian Danilo Gallinari First? | website=[[CBS News]] }}</ref>

Aside from basketball, Gallinari has worked as a model for [[Armani]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://vglmen.blogspot.com.au/2011/04/danilo-gallinari-for-armani-ea7.html |title=Danilo Gallinari for Emporio Armani EA7 |access-date=2014-01-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160817084842/http://vglmen.blogspot.com.au/2011/04/danilo-gallinari-for-armani-ea7.html |archive-date=2016-08-17 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
